sentences.text:
The petitioners are before this Court calling in question proceedings in C.C.No.16951/2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('IPC' for short)
and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. During the pendency of the petition, the husband and the wife, who were before the Family Court in M.C.No.4019/2021 have settled the dispute by drawing up of certain conditions of settlement and have filed an application under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C. supported by the affidavit of the husband.
Respondent No.2 -complainant is present in person.
One such condition towards the settlement of dispute between the parties is its closure of the present proceedings.

The said condition reads as follows:
"4. In view of the above settlement both the parties have agreed few terms between them as follows:
i) The petitioner has agreed to pay an amount of Rs.30,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty Lakhs Only) to the respondent towards maintenance/permanent alimony as full and NC: 2023:KHC:24914 final settlement of all her claims.

The petitioner has agreed to pay the said amount by way of demand draft bearing No.187049 dated 12.12.2022 drawn on Canara Bank, Bengaluru and the same will be handed over at the time of acceptance of the settlement by the Hon'be court.
ii) Both the parties states that they have exchanged all their belongings and they have no claims against each other in respect of moveable and the immoveable properties belonging to them.

iii) The respondent has agreed to settle/cooperate with the petitioner in seeking quashing of the proceedings in C.C. No.16951/2020 pending before V ACMM,
Bengaluru and pending in Crl.P No.1858/2021 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru.
5. Both the parties state that there is no collusion between the parties.
6. Both the parties state that they shall not interfere in each other's lives for any reason in the future.
3. In the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties and the offence being one punishable under Section 498A and 34 of the IPC, I deem it appropriate to close the proceedings.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following ORDER I. Criminal Petition is disposed.
NC: 2023:KHC:24914 II.
The proceedings in C.C.No.16951/2020 pending on the file of V Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru stand quashed qua the petitioners.
